name: whatsapp-mcp
cost: Free (MIT). It runs on a Cloudflare Workers Paid plan, which the README puts at a few dollars a month
works_with: Claude Code, Claude Desktop and any MCP client
short: A small server in your own Cloudflare account that lets your AI agent search and read your WhatsApp chats. It can't send messages.
what: You deploy it to your own Cloudflare account and link your phone to it once, the way you'd link WhatsApp Web. After that, your agent can list chats, read one chat, search across all of them and save names for phone numbers. It doesn't stay connected. It connects when your agent asks for something and once a day, collects what WhatsApp queued, stores it and hangs up. Your messages sit in a SQLite database in your Cloudflare account.
who: People who want an agent to answer questions about their own WhatsApp history, like what someone said about the flights. It is for one person and one WhatsApp account per deployment. If you're not comfortable deploying to Cloudflare from a terminal, or with an unofficial WhatsApp connection, skip it.
needs: A Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan

steps.title: Clone and install
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/finereli/whatsapp-mcp
cd whatsapp-mcp
npm install

steps.title: Create the token store
steps.text: Paste the id it prints into `wrangler.jsonc`.
steps.code: npx wrangler kv namespace create OAUTH_KV

steps.title: Set a password
steps.text: It protects the page that links your phone. Use 12 or more characters.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.text: Wrangler prints your URL, something like `https://whatsapp-mcp.your-name.workers.dev`.

steps.title: Link WhatsApp
steps.text: Open your URL and scan the QR code in WhatsApp under Settings, Linked Devices, Link a Device. On the phone itself you can use the phone number option instead. The first link imports your history, and you can close the page while it runs.

steps.title: Connect your agent
steps.text: In Claude Code, run this, then type `/mcp` and sign in with your password. Point other clients at the same `/mcp` URL.
steps.code: claude mcp add --transport http whatsapp https://your-url/mcp

try.label: From the README
try.text: Summarize what I missed in the family group this week.

watch: It isn't official. It uses the WhatsApp Web protocol through the Baileys library, which the README says is against WhatsApp's terms. The author calls the risk low for a read-only linked device, but not zero.
Each deployment holds your full message history and a live login to your WhatsApp account.
The first import is whatever history WhatsApp hands a new device. It may not be everything, and it only happens once per link.
Photos, voice notes and documents show up only as labels like `[image]`. Nothing is downloaded or transcribed.
The author hasn't tried the free Workers plan. On it, the README says to remove the `limits` block and expect the first import to be fragile.
Some chats show up as phone numbers. Your agent can fill in names using a contacts tool it already has.
